prompt.en: Which two-metre emergency-coverage plan should be rejected rather than treated as a dependable primary path?

text.en: A tested line-of-sight relay path with assigned operators and a fallback frequency.
A repeater plan with simplex fallback and a recent coverage check.
A plan that depends on future sporadic-E, auroral, or meteor openings appearing on schedule.
A ridge-top temporary station that was checked from both served sites.

explanation.en: Routine coverage should rest on tested ordinary paths and fallbacks. Unusual openings are useful opportunities, but they are not a schedulable primary service path.

prompt.en: A VHF event shifts from brief shower-related pings to a steadier path along a lake inversion. Which operating adjustment best fits the change?

text.en: Schedule long overs for the pings, because short reflections leave more time than inversion paths.
Treat the ping period as short contact windows, then use more normal exchange timing while the inversion path stays steady.
Log both as the same kind of ionospheric opening because the band is VHF.
Ignore timing once the first contact is made; both openings should last the same length.

explanation.en: Meteor-related pings are brief, so timing must be concise. A duct or enhanced lower-atmosphere path can allow more normal exchanges while the weather structure persists, but it still may fade.

prompt.en: After an unusual contact, which report best separates observation from diagnosis?

text.en: It was weak, so it was definitely ground wave and no other details matter.
It was distant, so all future contacts on the band can be scheduled daily.
Log the band, direction, duration, signal character, and weather or sky clues, then mark the mode as suspected if the evidence is incomplete.
If a signal is smeared, widen the transmitted signal before recording anything else.

explanation.en: Good notes keep observations separate from certainty. Band, direction, duration, signal quality, and environmental clues help identify a mode later without turning a guess into a guarantee.
